## Design objective
Transform the SignalRankAI user experience into a polished, responsive, evidence-first trading workspace inspired by the CRILOX design-motion references, **without producing imaginary trades or bypassing backend risk controls**.

## Correct integration target
This PR deliberately targets `design/signalrank-ui-rebuild-20261008` (existing Next.js integration PR #190), not production `main`. Live production still serves `web/platform_app`, while `frontend` on main is an untouched Next.js starter. The existing integration branch has the account-scoped fetch, MFA, billing, broker and paper workflows that must not be replaced with disconnected mock data.

## Implemented
- Rebuilt public homepage in `frontend/src/app/page.tsx` as a cinematic emerald, graphite and silver terminal with architectural hierarchy, meaningful schematics, responsive CTA/marketing navigation and truthful copy. No displayed prices, P&L, broker fills, success rate, or live market status are invented.
- Added `SignalLifecycleExperience` with a sticky four-gate illustration (source freshness → strategy/model → risk/admission → account-entitled receipt). A stage changes through IntersectionObserver and operable click controls; reduced-motion fallback, keyboard interaction and no-canvas presentation.
- Added last-loaded scoped `cinematic.css` styling public pages, the logged-in AppShell, real account metric/data cards, responsive navigation, market tables, mobile surfaces and login. Root theme control and existing API/CSRF semantics remain unchanged.
- Created reusable `SiteCredit`: **Powered by [CRILOX Solutions](https://www.criloxsolutions.com)**, integrated in the homepage, public editorials, authenticated workspace footer and primary sign-in page. Opens securely in a new tab.
- Added matching credit and minimal visual refinement to the existing serving legacy `web/platform_app` until a full replacement is certified. No legacy JS or broker behavior was changed.
- Added `frontend/scripts/cinematic-contract.test.mjs` and included it in the frontend presentation test script to pin truthful labels, meaningful stage navigation, all link destinations, shared attribution, data ownership boundaries, mobile rules and reduced-motion support.
- Retained actual SignalRank brand icon and green/silver identity instead of using CRILOX's separate cyan/lilac branding.

## Safety
- No order endpoints, kill switches, automatic trading, authorization logic, database migrations, Redis state, secrets, billing charges or performance/calibration logic modified.
- All authenticated balances/signals/probabilities remain sourced from the canonical API; if unavailable or unauthorized, the UI must fail closed.
- The visual diagrams are **illustrative, not live market data**; never show fake trading statistics.

## Mandatory remaining gates
1. Exact-commit frontend test suite: Node 22 / npm 11; `npm ci && npm run test:presentation && npm run test:transport && npm run test:dependencies && npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build`.
2. Authenticated browser QA against an **isolated staging API**, including login/MFA, role-dependent views, signal history evidence, paper orders, broker cert boundaries, notifications, billing, Telegram parity, recovery and negative/error states.
3. Check 320/375/430/768/1024/1440/1920 width layouts, WCAG color contrast at rest and focus, keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, and scroll-stage behavior.
4. Reconcile with recovery PR #189, #190 governance manifest generation and source/release policies; do not merge into production until all authorizations and soak evidence pass.
5. Verify licensing and available product assets if later augmenting with real case study screenshots; no third-party designs cloned.

**No production promotion is authorized by this PR.** Source code work is not proof that all backend workflows have been certified.

- **DO NOT PROMOTE** until exact-commit frontend tests, browser device QA, isolated staging/API session proof and governance/release evidence pass.

# Container security acceptance, 11 October 2026

The isolated Railway staging runtime for commit
`1cc4e556004e81614c8afe5befee0afc12304be8` was scanned with checksum-verified
Trivy 0.75.0 against its actual Debian 13.7 package inventory. The scan covered
Debian OS packages and reported 48 HIGH package/advisory rows. It did not certify
Python dependencies, native applications, broker behavior, or live execution.

Both application Dockerfiles now explicitly install the Debian security versions
of OpenSSL (`3.5.7-1~deb13u3`) and PCRE2 (`10.46-1~deb13u3`) in both stages.
The base-image digest and non-root runtime identity remain pinned. The replacement
image must be built and rescanned before these four fixable rows can be closed.

Primary references:

- [OpenSSL / DSA-6531-1](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-84782)
- [PCRE2 / DSA-6530-1](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-103111)

The original scan also reported unfixed stable-Debian findings in util-linux,
ACL, ncurses, systemd and Perl packages. Debian currently classifies several as
minor issues or postponed updates. Those classifications do not erase the
scanner findings or establish application-level non-exploitability. Do not mix
unstable Debian packages into the production runtime to force a clean scan.

The corresponding acceptance remains **BLOCKED**, with no vulnerability
suppression or fabricated fixed versions. An advisory-only source deployment,
if explicitly performed, must retain this limitation in its evidence and keep
financial execution disabled. It is not a security or live-money certification.
The mobile dependency audit separately retains four HIGH rows, including
node-forge; native release acceptance also remains blocked.

The hosted CI retry for the preceding commit did not start because GitHub
reported a billing lock. Independent local checks and Railway image build checks
are separate evidence; neither may be reported as a passing hosted CI run.

Delayed background delivery could consume the next scanner cycle's candidates or release its lock. Model promotion could also use a stale candidate/champion review, accept the text `"false"` as approval evidence, or classify nonfinite metrics as valid qualification. This recovery binds delivery to its originating cycle, protects reviewed registry snapshots transactionally, and makes model qualification fail closed on invalid evidence and metrics. Fresh provider candles also require the engine's canonical market session to be open before class certification can pass.

Retry selection prioritizes fresh qualified work before bucket deduplication and limits, defers stale housekeeping when fresh work exists, and validates shared opportunity state before recipient database work. Every eventual send retains fresh-quote, entitlement, terms, quota, profile and deduplication checks. Admission thresholds and customer terms were not weakened.

ML promotion compares candidate and primary row IDs, artifact digests and qualification-metadata fingerprints under row locks. Same-byte successor rows and in-place metadata edits cannot borrow a previous review; the actual payload and its parent must match the reviewed identities. Qualification requires actual boolean evidence and an enabled comparison appropriate to the primary's presence. Offline/comparison metrics, thresholds and tolerances reject NaN, Infinity, malformed/boolean values and invalid ranges. Existing human/schema gates remain, with finite registry query/commit budgets.

The cumulative branch also preserves immutable outcome datasets/component inputs, prospective universe observations, actual-writer savepoint recovery, governed trial/health evidence and bounded data-only SDK consumers. Historical publication, feature/repainting, instrument execution/capacity and broader acceptance remain open.

Validation for **0a5eafb837061d68465ebd9eec628d4edad639d6** (tree **b95999d5ece5c181b5a59939594968e947c13565**, clean unchanged source):

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |

Startup was exhausting PostgreSQL client slots while multiple subsystems initialized concurrently (worker/outcome tracker, ML load, and bot scheduler/webhook setup), triggering `asyncpg.exceptions.TooManyConnectionsError` and bot setup failures. This PR reduces default connection fan-out and caps scheduler jobstore DB usage so startup remains within DB limits.

- **DB engine default budget reduction**
  - Lowered async SQLAlchemy defaults in `db/session.py`:
    - `DB_POOL_SIZE`: `15 -> 5`
    - `DB_MAX_OVERFLOW`: `5 -> 3`
  - Applied consistently across both engine creation paths and startup pool-size logging.

- **Scheduler jobstore connection isolation + cap**
  - Updated `signalrank_telegram/bot.py` SQLAlchemyJobStore initialization to use explicit `engine_options` with conservative defaults:
    - `BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_SIZE=1`
    - `BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=0`
    - `BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30`
    - `BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_RECYCLE_SECONDS=1800`
    - `pool_pre_ping=True`
  - This prevents APScheduler’s sync jobstore from competing aggressively with core async runtime pools during startup.

- **Operational docs alignment**
  - Updated Railway baseline docs to reflect hardened pool defaults (`5/3`) so config guidance matches runtime behavior:
    - `docs/RAILWAY_GO_LIVE_CHECKLIST.md`
    - `docs/RAILWAY_VARIABLE_MATRIX.md`

- **Guardrail for future regressions**
  - Added/updated monolith hardening test to assert default async DB pool sizing remains at `pool_size=5` and `max_overflow=3`.

```python
# signalrank_telegram/bot.py (new SQLAlchemyJobStore cap)
_jobstore_engine_options = {
    "pool_size": max(1, _env_int("BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_SIZE", 1)),
    "max_overflow": max(0, _env_int("BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW", 0)),
    "pool_timeout": max(1, _env_int("BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 30)),
    "pool_recycle": max(30, _env_int("BOT_SCHEDULER_DB_POOL_RECYCLE_SECONDS", 1800)),
    "pool_pre_ping": True,
}
_jobstores["persistent"] = SQLAlchemyJobStore(
    url=_sched_sync_url,
    engine_options=_jobstore_engine_options,
)
```
title: Harden startup DB connection budgets to prevent `too many clients already` during monolith boot

Users reported the engine stopping after early cycles and not delivering signals. This PR targets freeze/stall points in the cycle pipeline and makes signal dispatch behavior explicit when consensus is empty.

- **Cycle-stall prevention in engine delivery path**
  - Removed blocking live-price fetch/enrichment work from the per-user `deliver_all()` async loop.
  - Switched delivery-time price handling to cached cycle prices (`_live_price_cache` / existing `current_price`) to avoid event-loop starvation.

- **Bounded `run_sync` boundaries**
  - Added timeout to `run_sync(deliver_all())` using `DELIVER_ALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default `180s`).
  - Added timeout to batch cooldown pre-check: `run_sync(_batch_cooldown_check(), timeout=15.0)`.

- **Consensus gating made explicit**
  - Replaced implicit hard behavior with explicit toggle:
    - `CONSENSUS_BLOCK_ON_EMPTY` controls whether empty-consensus blocks asset processing.
    - Falls back to `PROD_MODE` when unset.

- **Pipeline correctness / observability cleanup**
  - Removed duplicated consensus stats increment (`pipeline_stats["consensus"]` double-count).

- **Non-blocking freshness filter in Telegram dispatch**
  - Replaced sync-style enrichment/staleness checks in `dispatch_signals_async()` with async freshness validation via `validate_signal_freshness(...)`.
  - Reuses cached `current_price` when present and attaches validated live price to payloads.

```python
# engine/core.py
dispatched = run_sync(
    deliver_all(),
    timeout=float(_env_float("DELIVER_ALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 180.0)),
)

# engine/core.py
_cooled_down_pairs = run_sync(_batch_cooldown_check(), timeout=15.0)

# engine/core.py
_block_on_empty_consensus = _env_bool(
    "CONSENSUS_BLOCK_ON_EMPTY",
    _env_bool("PROD_MODE", False),
)
if not consensus_signals and _block_on_empty_consensus:
    continue
```

def _resolve_timeframes(env_key: str) -> list[str]:
    raw = os.getenv(env_key, _tf_default)
    parsed = _normalize_tf_list(raw)
    filtered = [tf for tf in parsed if tf in _allowed_tfs]
    if filtered:
        return filtered
    return [tf for tf in _normalize_tf_list(_tf_default) if tf in _allowed_tfs]

Three independent runtime errors were preventing signal engine startup, Telegram bot initialization, and ML model training. All three stem from bad file state (corrupted escape sequences, stray character) plus a schema/ORM drift.

## Syntax Fixes

**`engine/risk.py`** — The entire file contained `\"` (literal backslash + double-quote) instead of `"`, causing a `SyntaxError` at line 22 on every import. Replaced all occurrences with plain `"`. This was blocking `engine.core` from importing, so the signal engine loop was unconditionally skipped at startup.

**`signalrank_telegram/admin_commands.py`** — Stray `+` on its own at line 233 caused a `SyntaxError` that prevented the Telegram bot module from loading, silently disabling the webhook.

## Import Error Handling (`railway_main.py`)

The `run_bot` import error handler was swallowing failures and returning `None, False`, hiding the real cause. Changed to `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` + `raise` so bot import failures are fatal and surfaced immediately in logs rather than producing a confusing "started=False" with no traceback.

```python
# Before: silent failure
except Exception as exc:
    logger.warning(f"[bot] Could not import run_bot: {exc}; skipping webhook setup")
    return None, False

# After: loud failure with full context
except Exception as exc:
    logger.error("[bot] Fatal import error ...", exc, exc_info=True)
    raise
```

## Schema/ORM Alignment

**`db/migrations/versions/0014_add_outcome_pnl_pct.py`** — The `Outcome` ORM model defined `pnl_pct` but the `outcomes` table (created in `0001_init.py`) never included the column, causing `ProgrammingError: UndefinedColumn` whenever `ml/train_model.py` executed `SELECT … FROM outcomes` via the ORM.

Migration adds:
```sql
ALTER TABLE outcomes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pnl_pct FLOAT;
```

**`db/models.py`** — `Outcome.pnl_pct` changed from `Mapped[float]` (non-nullable) to `Mapped[Optional[float]]` so existing rows without a value don't produce constraint violations after the migration applies.

## Test Fix

`tests/test_risk_dynamic.py::test_risk_check_high_vol` was setting `volatility=0.15` but `risk_check` reads `atr_rel` first in an `or`-chain, so the high-volatility path was never exercised. The test was hidden behind the syntax error and silently never ran. Fixed to set `atr_rel=0.15`.

This PR replaces static proxy selection with a dynamic proxy lifecycle: fetch proxies from a provider, validate against Binance ping with strict timeout, persist health in Postgres, and serve low-latency rotation from Redis. - **Schema + migration: proxy inventory/health state**

This PR reduces dispatch latency risk and makes data-provider routing deterministic under real deployment conditions.

  - Added round-robin proxy selector from `PROXY_LIST` in `utils/proxy_manager.py`.
  - Wired proxy selection into shared async HTTP transport and provider connectors (Binance, Bybit, Polygon, TwelveData, CryptoCompare).
  - Updated shared client cache keying to include `provider + proxy` to avoid cross-provider client reuse ambiguity.

- **Thread-safe proxy state/caching**
  - Made proxy selection state lock-protected.
  - Cached parsed `PROXY_LIST` with env-change invalidation to avoid reparsing on each request and to keep rotation stable.

```python
# utils/proxy_manager.py
def _next_proxy() -> Optional[str]:
    with _LOCK:
        raw = (os.getenv("PROXY_LIST") or "").strip()
        if raw != _PROXY_CACHE_RAW:
            _PROXY_CACHE_RAW = raw
            _PROXY_CACHE_LIST = _parse_proxy_csv(raw)
            _INDEX = 0
        if not _PROXY_CACHE_LIST:
            return None
        idx = _INDEX % len(_PROXY_CACHE_LIST)
        _INDEX = (_INDEX + 1) % len(_PROXY_CACHE_LIST)
        return _PROXY_CACHE_LIST[idx]
```

Railway executes `startCommand` in exec form (not via `sh -c`), so leading `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 PYTHONMALLOC=malloc ...` tokens were treated as `argv[0]`, producing `The executable 'malloc_arena_max=2' could not be found`. These env vars were already declared in `nixpacks.toml [variables]` and injected automatically — the prefix was redundant and fatal.

- **`railway.json`** — `startCommand` changed from the broken prefixed invocation to `"bash start.sh"`, which delegates to the existing script that correctly calls `exec uvicorn railway_main:app`
- **`nixpacks.toml`** — `[start] cmd` stripped of all `VAR=value` prefixes; updated to `exec /opt/venv/bin/python -m uvicorn railway_main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8000}`. Updated comment explicitly warns against re-adding inline assignments
- **`tests/test_container_startup_cmd.py`** — regression test that parses both config files and asserts no start command begins with an `IDENTIFIER=value` token

+"startCommand": "bash start.sh"

Two production issues logged on 2026-04-06: repeated `RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown` from APScheduler, and `POST /telegram/webhook → 404` despite the bot reporting webhook readiness.

## APScheduler shutdown race

`signalrank_telegram.bot._bot_scheduler` (a `BackgroundScheduler` with its own `ThreadPoolExecutor`) was never explicitly shut down in the Railway lifespan `finally` block. Python's atexit handlers killed the executor first; the scheduler's background thread then tried to submit pending jobs into the dead pool.

- **`railway_main.py`**: lifespan `finally` block now shuts down `_bot_scheduler` before atexit fires:
  ```python
  _bot_sched = getattr(_bot_mod, "_bot_scheduler", None)
  if _bot_sched is not None and getattr(_bot_sched, "running", False):
      _bot_sched.shutdown(wait=False)
  ```
- **`signalrank_telegram/bot.py`**: `BackgroundScheduler` now constructed with `job_defaults = {coalesce: True, max_instances: 1, misfire_grace_time: 60}` to collapse cascaded misfires during startup lag or container restarts. Added structured log lines around scheduler creation and `start()`.

## Telegram webhook 404

When `RUN_ALL=true` (`start.sh`) or `RUN_MODE=all` (`main.py`), the old implementation spun up three separate `python main.py` processes. The web process served `web.app:app` — which has no `/telegram/webhook` route. The bot process auto-detected `RAILWAY_SERVICE_NAME`, enabled webhook mode, and registered the URL with Telegram. Every subsequent Telegram POST hit `web.app:app` and got 404.

- **`start.sh`**: `RUN_ALL=true` now runs `exec uvicorn railway_main:app` instead of three separate per-mode processes. `railway_main:app` owns the `/telegram/webhook` route and manages all subsystems in one event loop.
- **`main.py`**: `RUN_MODE=all` delegates to `railway_main:app` via uvicorn (matching what `start.sh` already did for that case). Removed the old `_run_all()` implementation that launched `web.app:app`.

## Tests

Three regression tests added to `tests/test_railway_lifecycle.py`:
- `test_webhook_route_registered_in_railway_main_app` — `POST /telegram/webhook` must not return 404
- `test_bot_background_scheduler_shut_down_during_lifespan_shutdown` — lifespan shutdown calls `shutdown(wait=False)` on `_bot_scheduler`
- `test_bot_scheduler_job_defaults_coalesce_and_misfire_grace_time` — verifies `coalesce=True` and `misfire_grace_time≥60` are present in `bot.py` source

In a single-service Railway deploy, signals were generated by the engine but never tracked to terminal outcomes and outcome notifications were never sent — because three Railway-specific env defaults silently disabled the worker loop and outcome tracker at startup.

## Root cause

`railway_main.py` defaulted `RUN_WORKER_LOOP` to `"0"` when `RAILWAY_SERVICE_NAME` was set, and `worker/worker.py` defaulted `WORKER_OUTCOME_TRACKER_ENABLED` to `False` on Railway. The `RealtimeOutcomeTracker` (15s TP/SL polling loop) therefore never ran.

body:
Bot was alive (heartbeat/webhook working) but signals were never delivered, dashboard callbacks silently failed, and the engine wasted cycles on signals no tier could ever receive. Root causes: wrong start command, stale threshold too tight for crypto, score gate below all tier thresholds, per-signal N×DB queries, and silent nav callback exceptions.

## Deployment entrypoint
- `nixpacks.toml` start command changed from `python main.py` → `uvicorn railway_main:app` — `[start]` overrides `railway.json` on Nixpacks builder; `main.py` alone never started the bot or scheduler
- Alembic removed from build phase; build containers have no `DATABASE_URL` so the migration silently no-ops. Migrations run exclusively via `run_startup_ops()` in the FastAPI lifespan

## Env var defaults baked into code
| Variable | Old default | New default |
|---|---|---|
| `DRY_RUN` | implicit `False` | explicit `'0'` |
| `RESEND_INCLUDE_FREE` | `'0'` | `'1'` |
| `SIGNAL_COOLDOWN_MINUTES` | `60` | `30` |
| `STALE_PRICE_THRESHOLD_PCT` | `'0.5'` | per-class (see below) |
| `TELEGRAM_USE_WEBHOOK` | unset | auto-`'1'` when `RAILWAY_SERVICE_NAME` present |
| `GEMINI_REVIEW_ENABLED` | already `'1'` | confirmed `'1'` |

## Stale signal validator (P3)
- Per-asset-class drift thresholds replace the flat 0.5% global: crypto **2.0%**, stock **1.0%**, commodity **0.8%**, FX **0.3%**. A full engine cycle takes 30–120 s; 0.5% on BTC/ETH invalidated every signal before delivery.
- `validate_signal_freshness` accepts `cached_live_price=` — skips HTTP call when price is already known
- `PRICE_DRIFT_TOLERANCE` in `tier_constants.py` synced to match

## Engine score gate (P4)
`MIN_SCORE_THRESHOLD` default **65 → 70** to match the lowest tier delivery gate (PREMIUM = 70). Signals scored 65–69 were stored and consumed cooldown slots yet were unreachable by every tier. Tier gates themselves are **unchanged** (FREE=80, PREMIUM=70, VIP=75).

## Performance: batch operations (P7 + P11)

**Before** — N blocking calls inside the signal loop:
```python
# Per-signal DB cooldown query (×N signals)
_dup_sig = run_sync(_check_cooldown())

# Per-signal HTTP price fetch in deliver_all
_fresh, _reason, _price = validate_signal_freshness_sync(_sig)
```

**After** — one query + one concurrent gather before the loop:
```python
# One query, O(1) set lookup per signal
_cooled_down_pairs = run_sync(_batch_cooldown_check())

# All unique assets fetched concurrently once
_price_results = await asyncio.gather(*[
    asyncio.wait_for(_get_live_price_async(a), timeout=5.0)
    for a in _unique_assets
], return_exceptions=True)
# Confirmed price stamped on signal dict → reused by _check_entry_status
```

## Dashboard callbacks (P6)
All `nav_*` handlers (`nav_home`, `nav_signals`, `nav_account`, `nav_performance`, `nav_upgrade`, `nav_support`) were swallowing exceptions silently. Now log via `logger.exception` and call `query.answer("⚠️ Something went wrong", show_alert=True)`.

## Bot startup / `_check_entry_status` (P8 + P12)
- `_post_init` per-user `set_my_commands` loop moved to `asyncio.create_task(...)` — no longer blocks `app.initialize()` on large user bases
- `_check_entry_status` uses `signal["current_price"]` (set by batch prefetch) before falling back to a live `httpx` call; blocking `requests.get` removed

## Gemini (P9 + P10)
- 429 cooldown written to `runtime_state` on every trigger; restored from DB on first `_gemini_in_cooldown()` call per process — Railway redeploys no longer reset an active quota cooldown
- Weekly review job sends an HTML DM summary (win-rate, W/L, retrain status, review snippet) to all `OWNER_IDS` on completion

30 pytest tests were failing across multiple root causes: a `SyntaxError` blocking all collection, Python 3.12 async incompatibilities, broken mock patching patterns, incorrect signal filter thresholds, and misconfigured webhook handlers.

## Test Infrastructure
- **`conftest.py` + `pytest.ini`**: Add `asyncio_mode = auto`; add `pytest-asyncio>=0.23` to requirements so `@pytest.mark.asyncio` tests run without boilerplate
- **`tests/test_enterprise_features.py`**: Replace all `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete()` → `asyncio.run()` (Python 3.12 removed the default thread event loop)
- **`tests/test_connectors.py`**: Fix deprecated pandas freq `"H"` → `"h"`

## Production Bug Fixes

### `engine/core.py`
`await asyncio.wait_for(...)` used inside sync `main_loop` — was a `SyntaxError` that blocked all test collection. Replaced with `run_sync()`.

### `ml/inference.py`
Add missing `_env_bool()` helper that `MLFilter` was calling but never defined locally (defined only in `railway_main.py`).

### `signalrank_telegram/bot.py`
Add `id=`, `replace_existing=True`, `max_instances=1` to every `scheduler.add_job()` call. Without this, a persisted SQLAlchemy job store registers a second copy of each job on every restart, causing duplicate signal delivery and Telegram flood-control bans.

On startup, pre-clean the persistent SQLAlchemy job store by removing any job whose ID is not in the known named set. This purges stale UUID-keyed rows left over from older deployments that caused `resend_unsent_signals_job` to fire multiple times per second.

### `engine/ultra_quality_filter.py`
Score is now a hard gate (immediate reject before other checks). All 11 checks required (`min=8` → `required=11`) so bad R:R, choppy-market, and wrong-session signals are properly rejected.

### `data/market_data.py`
Move the 6-char alpha FX check before the USD-suffix check so `EURUSD` routes to `EURUSD=X` instead of `EUR-USD`:
```python
# Before (wrong order):
if s.endswith("USD") and s[3:] == "USD":  # catches EURUSD → EUR-USD ❌
    return f"{s[:-3]}-USD"
if len(s) == 6 and s[:3].isalpha() and s[3:].isalpha():
    return f"{s}=X"

# After (correct order):
if len(s) == 6 and s[:3].isalpha() and s[3:].isalpha():  # EURUSD → EURUSD=X ✓
    return f"{s}=X"
if s.endswith("USD") and len(s) > 3:
    return f"{s[:-3]}-USD"
```

### `engine/price_validator.py` + `core/tier_constants.py`
`is_signal_fresh()` was returning `True` for signals with no `created_at`. Changed to `False, "No creation timestamp"`. Reduced `MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS['crypto']` 1800 → 300 s so 10-minute-old signals are correctly stale.

### `data/connectors/polygon_adapter.py` + `twelvedata_adapter.py`
`get_client` and `retry_async` were captured at module import time, making `patch("utils.httpx_client.get_client")` in tests a no-op. Both now do a module-level lookup at call time (`import utils.httpx_client as _hc; _hc.get_client()`).

### `web/app.py`
`_handle_charge_success_recurring` and `_handle_payment_failed` both had `if ENGINE is None: return` guards that short-circuited before any DB work. Removed guards; changed `get_session()` calls to `import db.session as _db_session; _db_session.get_session()` so test patches of `db.session.get_session` are honoured.

### `signalrank_telegram/formatter.py`
Fix `_format_price()` to return `"N/A"` for `None`/zero instead of `"$0.0000"`. Rewrite FREE/PREMIUM/VIP signal templates to match the professional spec with correct RR fallback (`0` default → `None`).

### `db/session.py`
Add `connect_args={"timeout": 10}` to the asyncpg engine so connection attempts time out after 10 s instead of hanging indefinitely (fixes `/start` log freezing at "DB session open, querying user row" on Railway). Move `_schema_checked = True` to before the first `await` in the schema-migration block so concurrent coroutines entering `get_session()` while DDL is in progress skip the migrations instead of running them twice.

### `signalrank_telegram/commands.py` + `signalrank_telegram/bot.py` (callback diagnostics)
Add `logger.info("[callback] <name> user_id=…")` at the very top of every `CallbackQueryHandler` callback (`agree_terms`, `decline_terms`, `vip_waitlist_join`, `cancel_confirm`, `cancel_nevermind`, `signal_reaction`, `mt5_trade`, `check_outcome`) so every button press is immediately visible in Railway logs. `query.answer()` is now called unconditionally before any DB work so the Telegram spinner stops instantly regardless of DB latency.

## Bug 1 — `TP: $0.0000` and `RR: 1:0.0` (formatter.py)

### Root cause
In `format_signal_premium_new` and `format_signal_vip_new`, `rr_ratio` falls back to `0` instead of `None`:
```python

```
When both fields are `None` in the DB row, this evaluates to `0`, so `format_enhanced_signal_data` receives `rr=0` and the display shows `1:0.0`.

Similarly, `take_profit` is stored as a JSON string in the DB (`"[112.94]"`), but `_parse_tp_list` is only called in `format_signal_vip_new`. In `format_signal_premium_new`, the raw `take_profit` string is passed to `_format_price()` which can't parse it.

### Fix

- Always run `_parse_tp_list()` on `take_profit` in `format_signal_premium_new`.
- Guard against `None` / `"N/A"` in every `_format_price()` call.

## Bug 2 — Duplicate `resend_unsent_signals_job` every minute (bot.py)

### Root cause (confirmed by logs)
```
Running job "resend_unsent_signals_job ... next run at: 02:11:07 UTC"
Running job "resend_unsent_signals_job ... next run at: 02:11:06 UTC"
```
`run_bot()` calls `scheduler.add_job(resend_unsent_signals_job, 'interval', minutes=1, jobstore=_sa)` **without** `id=` or `replace_existing=True`. When the `persistent` SQLAlchemy job store already has a persisted row from a previous deployment, APScheduler adds a second anonymous job, resulting in two concurrent executions every minute. This cascades into 40-60 Telegram flood-control errors and a 268-second rate-limit backoff.

### Fix
Add `id=`, `replace_existing=True` to **every** `scheduler.add_job()` call so restarts are idempotent:
```python
scheduler.add_job(
    resend_unsent_signals_job,
    'interval', minutes=1,
    id='resend_unsent_signals',
    replace_existing=True,
    jobstore=_sa,
)
```
Also add `max_instances=1` to the flood-prone jobs.

---

## Bug 3 — `NameError: name '_env_bool' is not defined` (ml/inference.py)

### Root cause
`_env_bool` is defined in `railway_main.py` but `ml/inference.py` calls it as if it were a local function:
```python
if not _env_bool("ML_ENABLED", False):
```
### Fix
Define `_env_bool` directly inside `ml/inference.py` (it's a one-liner):
```python
def _env_bool(name: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
    raw = os.getenv(name)
    if raw is None:
        return bool(default)
    return raw.strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "y", "on"}
```

---

## Bug 4 — `RuntimeError('Event loop is closed')` in `send_free_delayed_summaries`

### Root cause
`send_free_delayed_summaries` runs inside `run_bot()`'s `BackgroundScheduler` thread. It tries to call `bot.send_message()` using the PTB `Bot` object from the main event loop, but by the time the background thread runs, the main loop may be different or closed. This is the source of all the `Event loop is closed` errors seen for users `2093024725`, `5671427734`, etc.

### Fix
Replace direct `bot.send_message()` calls in background-thread jobs with `run_sync(async_func())` using a fresh bot context, mirroring the pattern used in `_resend_unsent_signals_async`.

The trading bot is sending **stale signals** that are not based on the latest market values. Signals are generated but not refreshed with real-time prices before delivery. Several critical issues need to be fixed:

### Root Causes of Stale Signals

1. **No real-time price validation before delivery**: In `engine/core.py` (lines 817-897), signals are generated during the engine cycle but delivered to users without re-checking if the entry price is still valid against the current market price. The `deliver_all()` function just iterates `scored_signals_all` without price freshness checks.

2. **Engine cycle interval too long**: In `engine/loop.py` (line 126), `main_loop` uses `interval_seconds=300` (5 minutes default). Signals generated at the start of a cycle may be 5+ minutes old by delivery time.

3. **No candle staleness detection**: `data/fetcher.py`'s `fetch_market_data()` (lines 140-160) fetches candles but never checks if the most recent candle timestamp is fresh. If a provider returns cached/old data, the bot still generates signals from it.

4. **Signal entry price drift**: When a signal is generated with `entry=45000` but BTC has moved to `45500` by delivery time, the user receives a stale entry price. There's no mechanism to update the entry price to the current market price at delivery time.

5. **No live price feed for signal updates**: The `/signal` command in `signalrank_telegram/commands.py` (lines 1050-1114) has a `_current_price()` helper but it's only used for display, not for validating or updating signals before delivery.

### Required Fixes and Improvements

- Before delivering any signal to a user, fetch the **current market price** and validate:
  - Entry price is still within acceptable range (e.g., within 0.5% of current price for crypto, 0.2% for FX)
  - Stop loss hasn't already been hit
  - Take profit hasn't already been reached
  - If entry price has drifted, **update the signal** with the current price and recalculate SL/TP proportionally
- Add a `last_price_check` timestamp to signals and skip delivery if price check fails

#### 2. Signal Freshness & Staleness Detection
- Add a `max_signal_age_seconds` config (default: 180 for crypto, 300 for FX/stocks)
- Before delivery, check `signal.created_at` vs current time - skip if too old
- Add candle freshness validation in `fetch_market_data()` - reject candle data if the latest candle is older than 2x the timeframe interval
- Log staleness events for monitoring

#### 3. News-Aware Signal Updates
- When news affects a market, **proactively notify users** who received signals for that asset BEFORE the news occurred
- Implementation:
  - After fetching news sentiment via `data/news.py`'s `get_news_sentiment()`, check if any **active/open signals** exist for the affected asset
  - If news sentiment conflicts with signal direction (e.g., bearish news on a LONG signal), send an **alert update** to users who received that signal
  - Add a new function `check_news_impact_on_active_signals()` that:

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Comprehensive overhaul of SignalRankAI trading bot

This PR must fix ALL the issues below. No placeholder values, no stubs, no TODO comments. Every function must be fully implemented and working.

---

### 1. STALE SIGNALS — Fix real-time market data pipeline

**Problem:** `data/market_data.py` function `fetch_market_data_cached()` serves cached candles without checking staleness. Signals are generated on hours/days-old data.

**Fix required in `data/market_data.py`:**
- Add staleness detection: reject cached candles older than 2× the timeframe interval (e.g., for 1h TF, reject candles older than 2 hours)
- Make **Yahoo Finance (yfinance)** the PRIMARY data source for ALL asset types (crypto, FX, stocks, commodities)
- Keep Binance/Bybit as fallback for crypto, AlphaVantage as fallback for FX
- yfinance symbol mapping: crypto → "BTC-USD", FX → "EURUSD=X", stocks → "AAPL", commodities → "GC=F" (gold), "CL=F" (oil), "SI=F" (silver)
- Add OHLCV validation: ensure `high >= max(open, close)`, `low <= min(open, close)`, sorted by timestamp ascending
- Log warnings when falling back from yfinance to secondary sources

**Fix required in `engine/core.py`:**
- Line 343: Change `cycle_sleep_seconds = 10` to dynamic based on smallest timeframe in cycle (e.g., 1h TF → 300s sleep, 4h → 900s, 1d → 3600s). Make configurable via `ENGINE_CYCLE_SLEEP_SECONDS` env var.
- Add timestamp validation on fetched market data — skip any asset where the latest candle is older than 2× the timeframe interval
- Add a `data_age_seconds` field to each signal so users and logs can see how fresh the data is
- Remove the random signal delivery delay entirely (see bot.py fix below)

**Fix required in `core/trade_tracker.py`:**
- `price_hit_tp()` currently always returns `False` — implement real logic: compare current market price against trade.target (support list of targets for partial TPs)
- `price_hit_sl()` currently always returns `False` — implement real logic: compare current market price against trade.stop
- For long trades: TP hit when price >= target, SL hit when price <= stop
- For short trades: TP hit when price <= target, SL hit when price >= stop
- `update_trade_outcomes()` should remove closed trades from `open_trades_list`
- Use yfinance `Ticker(symbol).fast_info['lastPrice']` for real-time price checks, with Binance REST API as fallback for crypto

---

### 2. SIGNAL DELIVERY — Remove random delays, enforce tier limits

**Problem in `signalrank_telegram/bot.py`:** Around line 1005-1025, `_send_random_signals_immediately()` picks a random time 0-18 hours in the future. Signals generated at 8 AM may not arrive until 5 PM — completely stale.

**Fix required in `signalrank_telegram/bot.py`:**
- Remove ALL random delay logic for signal delivery
- Send signals immediately when generated
- Enforce tier-based daily limits during delivery:
  - **Free**: 2 signals per day maximum
  - **Premium**: 20 signals per day maximum  
  - **VIP**: unlimited (all qualifying signals)
- Track daily signal count per user in Redis (key: `signals_sent:{user_id}:{date}`, TTL 86400)

**Fix required in `signalrank_telegram/formatter.py` (or wherever signals are formatted):**
- **Free tier signal format** — show enough to demonstrate quality but lock key details:
  ```
  📊 Signal Alert (Free)
  
  Asset: BTCUSDT
  Direction: LONG ⬆️
  Timeframe: 4h
  Entry: $67,450.00
  Confidence: 78/100
  
  🔒 Stop Loss: Upgrade to Premium
  🔒 Take Profit: Upgrade to Premium
  🔒 Risk/Reward: Upgrade to Premium
  🔒 Analysis: Upgrade to Premium
  
  📈 Signals remaining today: 1/2
  
  /upgrade to unlock full signals
  ```
- **Premium tier** — show everything: entry, SL, TP (all levels), R:R ratio, confidence score, strategy name, regime, analysis summary
- **VIP tier** — same as Premium plus: ML probability, confluence score, entry zone (high/low), partial exit targets, position sizing suggestion

---

### 3. FIX ALL BROKEN COMMANDS

**`signalrank_telegram/commands.py` fixes required:**

#### `/referral` (invite_command) — ~line 1508
- Currently works for Postgres path but fallback path generates a dummy hash code without storing it
- Fix: ensure the fallback path also calls `get_or_create_referral_code` and shows progress correctly
- Show: referral link, current count, progress toward next reward (3 refs = 7 days premium)

#### `/referral_leaderboard` — ~line 260
- Queries table `referrals` but the actual table is `referral_attributions` (check `db/models.py`)
- Fix the SQL to use the correct table name matching the SQLAlchemy model
- Show top 10 referrers with their usernames (mask if no username: "User ***123")

#### `/referral_rewards` — ~line 296  
- Queries `referral_rewards` table — verify this matches the actual model name
- Fix: also show pending rewards and progress toward next reward

#### `/pricing` (pricing_command)
- Currently shows vague text. Replace with actual prices:
  ```
  💰 SignalRankAI Plans
  
  🆓 Free Plan
  • 2 signals per day
  • Entry price...
